- Uncovered claim 'The largest gaps were concentrated in newly assigned Enterprise territories' [PARAMETRIC]: AC2 uses gap_concentration with dimension=territory, which measures concentration of gaps across a dimension but has no way to distinguish 'newly assigned Enterprise' territories from any other territory type. The claim's substance requires the gaps to be concentrated specifically in newly-assigned Enterprise territories — a categorical qualifier on territory type that no existing check can express. The existing check CAN measure gap concentration but cannot verify the 'newly assigned Enterprise' attribute that is the substance of this claim. (consider check: gap_concentration)

- Uncovered claim 'Several AEs are over-indexed to mature accounts' [PARAMETRIC]: AC4 uses headcount_growth_placement, which measures where capacity/headcount growth was placed — it does not measure individual AEs' account portfolio composition. The claim's substance is that AEs' existing book-of-business is skewed toward mature accounts. unowned_account_share measures share of accounts without ownership, not the maturity concentration of an AE's portfolio. No existing check measures the proportion of mature vs. new accounts in an individual AE's assigned portfolio, which is the substance of this claim. (consider check: unowned_account_share)

Coverage guard: 2 note(s) - proceeding:

[note] Uncovered claim 'The largest gaps were concentrated in newly assigned Enterprise territories' [PARAMETRIC]: AC2 uses gap_concentration on dimension 'territory', which measures the concentration of gap magnitude among the bottom territories but cannot verify that those territories are 'newly assigned Enterprise' territories. The claim's substance requires the gap-concentrated territories to be newly-assigned Enterprise ones — a classification attribute that no existing check can express. The substance (that gaps concentrate in a specific territory class) is not measurable; the entity qualifier ('newly assigned Enterprise') is a VOCAB_GAP, but the coverage check itself cannot prove the claim's direction or that the concentrated gaps fall in that segment. No existing check ties gap concentration to territory-assignment-recency or Enterprise classification. (consider check: gap_concentration)

[note] Uncovered claim 'Several AEs are over-indexed to mature accounts' [PARAMETRIC]: AC4 measures unowned account share, which is not the substance of the claim. 'Over-indexed to mature accounts' means AEs' revenue/pipeline is disproportionately weighted toward mature (existing) accounts relative to new/whitespace potential. unowned_account_share measures accounts without an assigned owner, a different entity and metric. The correct check would measure the share of revenue or pipeline attributable to mature accounts per AE (or the maturity mix of each AE's portfolio), which is not expressible by any existing check. The claim's substance — disproportionate concentration in mature accounts — has no matching primitive. (consider check: unowned_account_share)
